whmBands2026_27.note: Rates and ceilings confirmed against the 2026-27 withholding schedule (NAT 75331). The four base amounts are still derived, not published: the ATO assessment-rate page stops at 2025-26 and Schedule 15 publishes coefficients rather than base amounts. Re-check once the assessment page picks up 2026-27.

foreignResidentBands2025_26.note: Applies to withholding when the employer is not registered as a WHM employer. No tax-free threshold, no Medicare levy.

noTfnWithholdingRate.note: 45 per cent, not 47. The extra 2 per cent Medicare component belongs to the resident no-TFN rate and WHMs sit outside it. The rate is long standing, but the cited schedule now serves the version effective 1 July 2026, so it no longer evidences the 2025 start date.

taxFreeThreshold.note: Reachable by a WHM only when they are an Australian tax resident AND hold the nationality of an NDA country. See eligibility.json.

medicareLevyRate.note: Foreign residents do not pay it. A resident WHM does, unless a Medicare Entitlement Statement supports an exemption.

daspWhmRates.note: The ATO states the rule more broadly than a contribution-date test: having held a WHM visa at any time puts the entire payment at 65 per cent, including super earned while working under a different visa, with no apportionment. An associated bridging visa counts as a WHM visa. The dedicated tax-rates page for DASP is a 404; the table lives on the DASP topic page cited here. The 1 July 2017 start date is not stated on that page and remains unsourced.

deductionSubstantiationThreshold.note: No receipts needed below this total, but the expense must actually have been incurred and the taxpayer must be able to explain how the figure was worked out. It is not a free 300 dollars.

laundryRates.note: The 150 dollar written-evidence threshold covers washing, drying and ironing. It does not extend to dry-cleaning.

residentBands2025_26.note: Identical to 2024-25 in every threshold, rate and base amount. The page prints the 2026-27 table above this one, so read by year and never by position. Base amounts are published for the third band and up; the second band is published only as "16c for each $1 over $18,200", which is a base of zero. Excludes the Medicare levy.

residentBands2026_27.note: The legislated cut takes the second band to 15c. Unlike the working holiday table for the same year, these base amounts are published rather than derived. Excludes the Medicare levy.

lowIncomeTaxOffset.note: Non-refundable: it reduces tax payable to zero and no further, and an unused part is not paid out. The ATO page states no income year; ITAA 1997 s 61-110 applies it to 2020-21 and later years and s 61-115 has not been amended since, which is what makes it good for both years here. Available in full to a part-year resident: s 61-110(1)(a) asks only for residency "at any time during the income year", so unlike the tax-free threshold it is not apportioned. Taper reaches zero at 66,666.67 while entitlement ceases above 66,667, so clamp at zero.

medicareLevyLowIncomeSingle2025_26.note: Single with no dependants and no seniors offset. Both comparisons are inclusive: no levy at or below the lower threshold, a reduction at or below the upper one, full two per cent only above it. The shade-in rate is not published anywhere on the ATO site, but the worked example on this page pins it exactly: a taxable income of 29,000 gives a levy of 98.90, which is ten cents in each dollar above 28,011. Thresholds are indexed annually and announced late; no 2026-27 table exists yet.

partYearTaxFreeThreshold.note: Someone who becomes a resident partway through the year gets 13,464 plus 4,736 apportioned over the months they were a resident, counting the month of arrival in full and running to 30 June. Staying resident to year end does not avoid the apportionment. Whole calendar months, no day-level proration: 31 January and 1 January both count six months. The two components sum to 18,200. The page carries no effective date; 2012-07-01 is when the 18,200 threshold began. No rounding rule is published for the months that do not divide evenly.
